title: Upstream review map
caption: What this repository offers for review, the order a credible upstream landing would take, and what stays downstream on purpose.

nodes.core: The reusable core. One crate that scans TSRX, builds the overlay, projects legal TSX, and lifts formatted output back. No OXC API dependency.
nodes.unicode: The core's only direct dependency: a standalone Unicode table for ECMAScript identifier semantics.
nodes.evidence: Grammar fixtures, Unicode boundary tests, layout freezes, and six benchmark families. Evidence travels with the code so review starts from facts.
nodes.adapter: All twelve canonical OXC dependencies sit behind one adapter crate pinned at one exact commit. This is the non-fork guarantee.
nodes.glue: Config discovery, CLI orchestration, npm wrappers, and the VS Code companion. Product glue that should stay out of OXC.
nodes.review: Step one is a design review, not a patch. Maintainers judge whether projected legal TSX is an acceptable first upstream architecture.
nodes.experiment: Step two moves scan, overlay, projection, mapping, and diagnostics into a maintainer-owned experimental crate, comparing allocations and throughput first.
nodes.contract: Step three gives Oxlint an explicit projected-source contract: authored path, virtual TSX, complete mapping data, and fix-safety rules.
nodes.strategy: Step four proves Oxlint diagnostics and fixes, then adds an Oxfmt strategy around the checked format projection and lift.
nodes.routing: Only after those paths exist should SourceType, FileKind, command routing, and LSP capabilities advertise .tsrx.

steps.label: Review the core
steps.caption: The ask is a design review of one small crate plus its evidence. Reading the core and its tests is the whole first step.

steps.label: Prototype
steps.caption: A maintainer-owned experimental crate adopts the scan, overlay, projection, and mapping work with performance compared before representation changes.

steps.label: Contract
steps.caption: Oxlint gets an explicit projected-source contract instead of squeezing TSRX into the contiguous-slice PartialLoader.

steps.label: One app at a time
steps.caption: Oxlint first, then Oxfmt, and only then do the app and editor layers advertise .tsrx.

steps.label: Stays downstream
steps.caption: The adapter pin and the product glue are not part of the proposal. They keep shipping here, and the companion surfaces retire only after released parity.
